meta.note: This file consolidates real corporate/industry names already documented elsewhere in this project (as lab sponsors in Lakshya 2047, as GCF Programme certification partners, and as Projections tech fest industry contributors) into an organized industry-academia partnership view, rather than restating them differently. It distinguishes genuine corporate/industry partnerships from government research funding bodies (DST/DBT/GUJCOST) and the academic publisher partnership (Springer Nature), which are real but not 'industry' in the corporate sense requested by this category.

mous_for_curriculum_collaboration.cross_reference: The GCF (Global Certification Forum) Programme, already documented in skill_development_certifications_parul_details.json, represents the clearest curriculum-integrated industry tie-up — IBM (Java, Python), Microsoft (Azure AI, Power Platform), AWS (Cloud Foundations), Cisco (Networking, Security), and Autodesk (AutoCAD, Inventor) certifications are woven into the six-semester structure rather than offered as a purely elective add-on.
mous_for_curriculum_collaboration.additional_addon_partners: The broader elective add-on certification list (already documented in academic_details_parul.json) adds Oracle and Adobe as further curriculum-adjacent industry partners.

guest_lecture_series_tie_ups.cross_reference: Already documented in events_fests_cultural_calendar_parul_details.json — the Projections technical fest has featured 15+ industry tie-ups and multiple guest lecture sessions from technology professionals in recent editions.
guest_lecture_series_tie_ups.additional_note: Beyond the annual fest, individual faculties organize their own guest lecture series throughout the year, already documented in placements_parul_details.json's career counseling and higher-studies support sections.

joint_research_collaborations.government_funded_research: Research funding partners documented in research_innovation_parul_details.json (DST, DBT, GUJCOST — Government of India/Gujarat science and technology bodies) are government research collaborations rather than corporate industry partnerships specifically.
joint_research_collaborations.academic_publishing_partnership: The Springer Nature partnership (already documented in research_innovation_parul_details.json) is a real international partnership, though it is an academic publishing collaboration rather than a corporate/industry research partnership.
joint_research_collaborations.honest_gap: A specific corporate-industry JOINT RESEARCH collaboration (as distinct from lab sponsorship or certification partnerships) was not independently confirmed in available research — the strongest documented industry ties are in lab sponsorship and certification programs, covered below and above.

corporate_sponsored_labs_and_centers.description: The university's lab ecosystem (Lakshya 2047, already documented in campus_facilities_infrastructure_parul_details.json) names multiple real corporate partners associated with specific labs:
named_corporate_lab_partners: AWS — Amazon Web Services (cloud computing-aligned lab)
corporate_sponsored_labs_and_centers.caution: As with the broader Lakshya 2047 description, these lab-partner associations were self-flagged as unverified in the original research (a relatively newly-described initiative) and should be confirmed with the university directly for current accuracy.
